text:
devon: Quick Q during the pricing slide — can someone clarify how rate limits vs quotas work for free trial customers?

mikey: short answer: rate limits are real-time throttles (requests/sec) applied per API key; quotas are longer-term usage caps (tokens/month). free trial gets both but with more generous quotas.

devon: thanks — does the trial quota include embeddings and chat equally, or are they separate buckets?

mikey: separate. embeddings and generation count against different quota lines. we also tier soft vs hard limits: soft = advisory + dashboard alerts, hard = requests rejected with 429.

alyssa: will the trial auto-upgrade when they hit quota or just stop? sales needs to know for onboarding flows.

jess: trial does NOT auto-upgrade. user sees a modal in the console + email with purchase links. we decided not to autopay to avoid surprise invoices.

devon: okay — what about rate limits on hosted vs dedicated customers? same policies?

mikey: hosted (Redwood API) enforces per-key rate limits and global region-level capacity signals. Dedicated customers get a separate model: we ship dedicated capacity with configured concurrency and TPS in the contract; there's still a soft enforcement layer in the control plane to protect the cluster.

katie: to add — for enterprise/private deployments customers can set their own limits via the console or policy API. our defaults are just safety nets.

devon: nice. one more: how do credits + promo codes interact with quotas (billing team asked)?

jess: credits are applied to the billing balance, they don't expand quota by default. we have a flaggable flow to convert credits -> temporary quota increase for specific customers (manual ops + sales approval).

alyssa: is there a self-serve option to buy more quota without changing billing terms? some trial-to-paid flows should be frictionless.

jess: yes — buying a monthly capacity add-on in the console increases quota immediately and charges to the card on file. contract upgrades still handled by sales for Dedicated.

devon: ok re: 429s — what error body do we return? we need it standard for SDKs to parse.

mikey: we return 429 with JSON: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after": seconds}. SDKs surface retry_after. will add docs snippet.

devon: can we include an example in the error doc? small code block to show header + body would help.

mikey: yup, leaving that as an action item for docs. @katie anything from leadership on raising quota limits for major pilot customers?

katie: leadership stance: be generous for pilots but instrument everything. if it's strategic, raise quotas manually + add a toast in console explaining the limits lifted. we want monitoring + an exit plan if usage spikes.

alyssa: noted. will add to onboarding checklist: signal to billing + solutions eng when quotas are bumped.

all-hands-bot: Reminder: follow-up items created — #1234 (docs: rate-limit examples), #1235 (onboarding checklist), #1236 (trial email copy).

devon: thanks all. small ask: can we surface trial remaining quota in the SDK responses so apps can show "X tokens left this month"?

mikey: good idea — feasibility: we can add an optional header X-Remaining-Quota and an endpoint /v1/usage for programmatic checks. will prototype.

jess: watch out for privacy/regulatory implications for shared keys. usage endpoint will require admin scopes.

devon: understood. that's fine. thanks everyone! :clap:

katie: great discussion — thanks for asking. we'll follow up in the doc thread and the items above.
